vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: mails-for-agent
Version: 1.6.0

The skill bundle provides a structured interface for an AI agent to interact with an email service via a REST API, supporting operations like sending/receiving emails, managing threads, and extracting verification codes. The instructions in SKILL.md are transparent, well-documented, and strictly aligned with the stated purpose of enabling email-based workflows. No evidence of malicious intent, data exfiltration, obfuscation, or prompt injection was found.

llm.summary: The skill's requested env vars, instructions, and lack of install steps align with its stated purpose (HTTP access to an email API); main remaining risk is trusting the remote email service and the auth token you provide.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (send/receive emails via HTTP API) match the declared requirements: MAILS_API_URL, MAILS_AUTH_TOKEN, MAILS_MAILBOX. No unrelated credentials, binaries, or config paths are requested. primaryEnv=MAILS_AUTH_TOKEN is appropriate.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md contains a focused HTTP API contract (endpoints, params, response shapes) and instructs use of only the declared environment variables. It does not instruct reading unrelated files, scanning system state, or transmitting data to other endpoints beyond MAILS_API_URL.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec and no bundled code — instruction-only skill. This is lowest-risk for persistence and code execution since nothing is written to disk by the skill itself.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Requires three env vars that are directly relevant (API base URL, bearer auth token, mailbox identifier). No extraneous secrets or broad system credentials are requested.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false and no install mean the skill does not force permanent inclusion. Model invocation is enabled (default), so an agent could autonomously call the mail API when this skill is used — this is normal but worth noting because it grants the agent the ability to send/delete/read mailbox data using the provided token.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears internally consistent and only needs an API URL, an auth token, and a mailbox address — which is expected for an HTTP email service. Before installing, verify you trust the MAILS_API_URL operator and that the MAILS_AUTH_TOKEN has minimal scope and an expiration if possible. Consider: (1) who runs the API and their privacy/security posture; (2) what the agent will be allowed to do with the mailbox (send, delete, read attachments) and whether you permit autonomous agent actions; (3) storing the token in a secure secret store and rotating it regularly; and (4) enabling logging/auditing or restricting the agent's capability if you want to limit automated signups or message deletion. If you need higher assurance, request the API's documentation or a known provider domain and check for TLS and scoped credentials.
